reason: The passage depicts Yahweh actively saving and protecting the Hebrew people from Egyptian slavery and military pursuit. God parts the sea for their safe passage (וּבְקָעֵ֑הוּ), provides protection via a cloud and pillar of fire (עַמּ֤וּד הֶֽעָנָן֙), and explicitly commits to fighting for them (יְהוָ֖ה יִלָּחֵ֣ם לָכֶ֑ם - 'Yahweh will fight for you'). The text concludes with Yahweh saving Israel from Egyptian hands (וַיּ֨וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יִם) while drowning their pursuers. These actions demonstrate protective, salvific intervention—the antithesis of antagonism.
